entry.title: An Exact QFT/Lattice Map for Fermions. We construct an exact map between continuum fermion fields and lattice fields in 1+1 dimensions.
entry.summary:
We construct an exact map between continuum fermion fields and lattice fields in 1+1 dimensions. This map rewrites a continuum Hamiltonian as a lattice Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor couplings and an infinite-dimensional local Hilbert space. The resulting lattice model reproduces exactly the energy spectrum, global operator algebra, chiral symmetries, and anomalies of the continuum QFT on any finite lattice.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #high-energy #post-quantum

entry.title: Quantum Advantage has Few Complexity Implications. We consider the complexity implications of proofs of quantumness and (quantum verifier) oblivious state preparation.
entry.summary:
We consider the complexity implications of proofs of quantumness and (quantum verifier) oblivious state preparation. We show that both of these objects can coexist with the easiness of nondeterministic computation. That is, we give evidence that proofs of quantumness can exist when $\mathsf{P} = \mathsf{NP}$ and that (quantum verifier) oblivious state preparation can exist when $\mathsf{BQP} = \mathsf{QCMA}$.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #algorithms #cryptography

entry.title: Minimal model of a Plateau-Rayleigh instability of a solid binary alloy nanowire: impacts of surface segregation
entry.summary:
Minimal model and its linear stability analysis (LSA) for Plateau-Rayleigh (PR) instability of an intermixed, solid binary alloy nanowire is presented. Model accounts only for the surface diffusions of the alloy components without anisotropies of a surface energies, and for a classical thermodynamic surface segregation. Model allows to assess a deviation of a longwave instability cutoff wavelength $λ_c$ from the classical value $2πr_0$ (a wire circumference) as a function of a surface composition deviation from its equilibrium value, a wire radius, and a bulk concentration of a minority component.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #clean-tech

entry.title: DynaMite: Dynamic Measurement Scheduling To Accelerate Fault-Tolerant Quantum Programs
entry.summary:
Fault-tolerant quantum computers run millions of logical cycles to perform quantum error correction (QEC). As logical operations span entire logical cycles, the logical cycle time (LCT) dictates program runtime. Qubit measurements, critical to extract parity information for QEC, are the slowest operations and account for 43-86% of LCT.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #computer-architecture #infosec

entry.title: Breaking the quantum barriers for Graph Collision
entry.summary:
In the graph collision problem, the task is to decide whether a known graph on $n$ vertices contains an edge with both endpoints marked, given query access to the input bits specifying the marked vertices. We first refute the conjectured $Ω(n^{2/3})$ query lower bound with a bounded error quantum algorithm using $\widetilde O(n^{92/139})$ queries. We then refine this approach to obtain a $\widetilde O(n^{11/17})$ query algorithm.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #quantum-computing #algorithms

entry.title: Quantum Query Lower Bounds from Classical Moment Matching. We prove a quantum analogue of the classical moment matching method, a popular framework used to prove lower bounds in property testing.
entry.summary:
We prove a quantum analogue of the classical moment matching method, a popular framework used to prove lower bounds in property testing. For two random variables $X_0$ and $X_1$ whose moments match up to the first $r-1$ moments, the classical moment matching method says that no classical algorithm can reliably distinguish between input instances of length $N$ constructed from $X_0$ and $X_1$, respectively, unless it performs at least $Ω(N^{1-1/r})$ queries. While this method has been widely explored since its inception in the seminal work of Raskhodnikova, Ron, Shpilka, and Smith (STOC 2007) to prove lower bounds for symmetric properties, it has remained an open question whether a quantum analogue of it could be proved.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #quantum-computing #algorithms
